svg.title: Thirty Days to a Measured, Contract-Ready Delivery System
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-thirty-day-launch-sprint; chart type: timeline_roadmap; title: Thirty Days to a Measured, Contract-Ready Delivery System; subtitle: Build the operating evidence before treating acquisition volume as progress.; chapter number: 12; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: The canonical time to first deal is 1-4 months. This sprint establishes readiness and pilot evidence; it does not assume a signed customer, completed provider response, or collected revenue within thirty days.; caption: Exit with traceable permissions, a reconciled sample cohort, a costed service scope, and explicit working-capital needs. Expand only against measured capacity and authorized live work.; stages: label: Days 1-7; value: Select one service niche and document the permitted contract structure; numeric value: 7.0; detail: Choose one counsel-defined exposure and evidence matrix. Draft fixed or cost-plus scope, jurisdictional rules mapping, defect definitions, and a 30-day contractual replacement window. Record the $705,000 Base revenue and $437,100 expense targets as annual planning figures.; label: Days 8-14; value: Configure provenance capture and test record-handling boundaries; numeric value: 14.0; detail: Test synthetic intake records through CRM permissions, contact suppression, duplicate checks, and invoice mapping. Verify authorization templates and approved storage. Demonstrate source-page citations and a manual exception route before allowing live record parsing.; label: Days 15-21; value: Run a bounded authorized pilot and measure retrieval loss; numeric value: 21.0; detail: After customer authorization, launch only the budgeted sample and log every cohort transition. Record provider outlays even when proof fails. If no customer has signed, continue synthetic workflow testing and prospect discussions rather than processing live claimant records.; label: Days 22-30; value: Reconcile service economics and publish the next operating decision; numeric value: 30.0; detail: Calculate duplicate loss, usable-proof yield, deficiency repair cost, and invoice aging. Keep pending provider requests out of completed-proof counts. Reconcile the six-bar Base bridge, stress one delayed monthly invoice, and set the next month's spend from signed scope and cash.
